title: The Choir of the Ninth Floor
premise: Mirabel Blackwood takes a teaching post at Halloway Preparatory, where students vanish from the ninth floor and the staff pretend not to notice. When an excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside beneath the school's foundations, Mirabel learns the missing class of 1974 never left—they were absorbed into the Choir, a chorus that keeps the building standing by singing its residents into the walls. As the harvest moon approaches and the Choir's conductor begins recruiting a new verse, Mirabel must choose between the found family of misfit teachers who shielded him and the truth that could free them all. In the end he sings the last verse without joining it, unmaking the door at the cost of his own voice, while the survivors walk out into a school that finally forgets how to sing.
about_author: Mara Zhou is the pen name of a former night-shift school custodian who spent three years collecting the strange maintenance logs of one particular building before writing fiction. She lives somewhere with good locks and no basements.

chapters.title: Orientation
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He arrives at Halloway Prep as the new literature teacher, counting doors out of nervous habit and noticing the ninth floor has no classroom numbers. The headmaster, Voss, gives him a keyring with one key that fits nothing. Emotional beat: uneasy new beginnings masked as routine.

chapters.title: The Missing-Class Problem
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. His roster lists thirty-one students; twenty-two show up. Colleagues deflect questions with practiced smiles. He finds a yearbook page where an entire class photo has been carefully inked over. Emotional beat: creeping wrongness beneath institutional politeness.

chapters.title: Lights On, Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Establishing his nightly ritual: checking every lock, leaving hallway lights burning because darkness on the ninth floor 'breathes.' Custodian Ruth teaches him the routes that are safe after ten p.m. Emotional beat: fragile control through ritual.

chapters.title: The Excavation Crew
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Construction begins on the annex; the crew hits something old beneath the gymnasium. That night, every counted door is open by exactly one inch. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: A Door Sealed from the Inside
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He descends to see the unearthed door—scratches on the inner face, claw-marks pointing outward-inward confusion, and a brass plate reading CHOIR ROOM. Ruth begs him to stop asking questions. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into fact.

chapters.title: Faculty Lounge Politics
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Mirabel and science teacher Devi Okafor. We learn the staff's unwritten pact: never mention the ninth floor, never learn names of the vanished. Devi quietly disagrees. Emotional beat: loyalty as complicity.

chapters.title: The Student Who Waved
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A girl appears in his classroom he's never enrolled—Tamsin, pale, always cold, gone by lunch. His attendance sheet shows her name in faded pencil, dated 1974. Emotional beat: grief for someone still technically alive.

chapters.title: Hymnal in the Walls
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. Renovations expose a cavity full of hymnals, each with verses added in children's handwriting—the song grows longer every decade. The last page holds a blank stave labeled 'the ninth verse.' Emotional beat: horror as scholarship.

chapters.title: Voss's Office Hours
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Headmaster Voss offers him tenure in exchange for signing a confidentiality addendum. Through the office wall, faintly, something hums in four-part harmony. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as kindness.

chapters.title: Ruth's Confession
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. The custodian admits she was a student in 1974; she was meant to be in the Choir but hid in the boiler room during roll call. She's kept the lights on ever since as penance. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt made structural.

chapters.title: Ninth Floor Field Trip
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Following Tamsin's trail, he reaches the ninth floor—a corridor of doors numbered like classrooms but opening onto the same small room, over and over. Something counts him back. Emotional beat: spatial horror, loss of orientation.

chapters.title: Found Family, Found Rules
chapters.summary: Ensemble scene, rotating POV among Mirabel, Devi, Ruth, and groundskeeper Hollis. Over contraband whiskey they form a pact to investigate together—four outsiders against an institution. Emotional beat: warmth as defiance.

chapters.title: The Conductor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. In the archive she finds ledgers listing every vanished student under 'Voices Retained,' signed by successive headmasters—including Voss's own mentorship signature. Emotional beat: betrayal by paperwork.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon Countdown
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Astronomical charts in the choir room show the ritual recurs each harvest moon; this year's falls in eleven days. Tamsin appears again, mouthing words: don't learn the last verse. Emotional beat: ticking clock established.

chapters.title: What the Walls Want
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. The building begins making demands—doors rearranging, hallways lengthening toward the excavation site. Ruth recognizes the architecture steering them like sheep. Emotional beat: the school as predator.

chapters.title: Voss Sings
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He catches Voss alone at dusk, humming the first eight verses flawlessly, eyes glazed. Voss explains, gently, that the Choir isn't punishment—it's permanence. No one at Halloway ever truly leaves. Emotional beat: seductive villainy.

chapters.title: Tamsin's Verse
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV (first ghost chapter). She remembers 1974: the field trip below, the door closing, the teacher who sang first so the children would follow. She's been trying to warn teachers for fifty years. Emotional beat: tragic witness.

chapters.title: The Key That Fits Nothing
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He realizes his mystery key matches the excavated door—not to open it, but to keep it shut. Someone intended a new keeper. Voss chose him deliberately. Emotional beat: chosen-ness as trap.

chapters.title: Loyalty Test
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The headmaster offers Devi her dream lab in exchange for reporting on Mirabel. She accepts the meeting—and records everything. Emotional beat: loyalty bending without breaking.

chapters.title: Halfway Down
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The quartet explores beneath the foundation: a mirrored version of the school, classrooms preserved mid-lesson, chalk dust suspended. They find the 1974 class seated, waiting, breathing. Emotional beat: awe curdling to terror.

chapters.title: Roll Call
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The seated students turn as one when he reads their names aloud—names give them a flicker of self. Tamsin nearly surfaces before the harmony swells and pulls her back down. Emotional beat: hope weaponized against them.

chapters.title: The First Betrayal
chapters.summary: Hollis's POV. Groundskeeper Hollis, revealed to have been feeding information to Voss for years to keep his son's name off the ledger, sabotages the group's maps. Emotional beat: love justifying treachery.

chapters.title: Quarantine
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. Voss locks down the school for 'asbestos remediation,' cutting phones. Parents' calls go to a cheerful recorded voice that hums between sentences. Emotional beat: isolation closing in.

chapters.title: Verse Nine, Partial
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In the hymnal cavity, the blank stave has begun filling itself in—his own handwriting. Learning the song is happening whether he consents or not. Emotional beat: erosion of self-determination.

chapters.title: Ruth Descends
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth goes down alone to bargain with the Choir using her fifty years of withheld service. She returns hollowed, able only to speak in rhyme. Emotional beat: sacrifice that buys time, not victory.

chapters.title: The Teacher Who Sang First
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The ghost chapter reveals Mr. Aldery, the 1974 teacher, still conducts from within—half-willing, half-consumed, keeping the children calm so they won't scream. He is the monster and the mercy both. Emotional beat: monstrous compassion.

chapters.title: Doors Counted Wrong
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. His nightly count comes up one door too many. Behind it: his own classroom, himself at the desk, already singing. Emotional beat: identity horror, the self as bait.

chapters.title: Split the Quartet
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Voss exploits Hollis's betrayal to isolate Devi and Ruth; Mirabel wakes locked in the annex with the excavated door humming beside him. Emotional beat: the found family fractured.

chapters.title: What Hollis Bought
chapters.summary: Hollis's POV. He visits his son's dorm room at another school and finds the boy humming verse one. The ledger doesn't forgive debts; it collects interest. Emotional beat: devastating realization that betrayal purchased nothing.

chapters.title: Convergence
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Harvest moon tomorrow. The whole school sleepwalks toward the gymnasium stairwell, staff included, drawn by a melody only half-heard. Mirabel resists by reciting his door-count like a counter-hymn. Emotional beat: ritual against ritual.

chapters.title: The Last Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss conducts the entranced faculty in a full run-through of eight verses; the building drinks the sound and visibly strengthens, walls knitting, the sealed door thinning. Emotional beat: power's grotesque vitality.

chapters.title: Aldery's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Below, Tamsin reaches what's left of Aldery. He tells her the escape clause: the ninth verse can be sung by a living voice that knows it fully but refuses to join—if sung from outside the circle, it unmakes the door and frees the retained. It will also take the singer's voice forever. Emotional beat: terrible hope.

chapters.title: Learning Without Singing
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Tamsin teaches Mirabel the ninth verse silently, mouth to ear, note by note, while he fights the urge to hum along—each near-slip physically dragging him toward the stairwell. Emotional beat: white-knuckle restraint.

chapters.title: Reunion of the Broken
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Devi breaks Ruth out of the infirmary; Hollis returns, confessing everything, offering his knowledge of the tunnels. The quartet reforms, scarred. Emotional beat: forgiveness as strategy and grace.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon Rising
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The moon clears the water tower. The door opens inward for the first time in fifty years, and the Choir begins to climb. Emotional beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: The Ninth Verse
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Climax. In the gymnasium, amid the ascending Choir, Mirabel sings the final verse aloud—alone, unjoined, voice cracking—as Voss screams counterpoint. The harmonies unravel; the retained students surface one by one; the door below slams shut forever, from neither side. Emotional beat: triumph paid in flesh.

chapters.title: Silence
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Aftermath: Mirabel mute, the school ordinary, Voss found catatonic, humming nothing. Tamsin and the freed class fade gratefully into morning light. Emotional beat: hollow, earned peace.

chapters.title: What Remains of Ruth
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth's speech returns word by word; she tends the graves finally dug for the class of 1974. She and Mirabel communicate in written notes—he writes beautifully now. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into tending.

chapters.title: Last Bell
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. The school reopens under interim administration; Devi burns the ledgers except one page kept as evidence. Hollis transfers away, forgiven but not forgotten. Emotional beat: institutions endure, people change them anyway.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Key
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Epilogue. Leaving Halloway, Mirabel drops his useless key into the filled excavation site. Deep below, faintly, something tries the first note of verse one—and finds no door to answer it. Emotional beat: quiet vigilance, a door closed but remembered.
